title: Keyframe Animation Improvement | Clo 2025.1 Features Deep Dives
description:
The new update to our keyframe animation in CLO 2025.1 allows you to apply keyframes to render lights and quickly adjust the animation playback range based on specific layers. 

Check out other new features here:https://clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord?utm_campaign=multi_item_banner_JointheOfficialCLODiscord&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio

summary: ```markdown # Keyframe Animation Improvement | Clo 2025.1 Features Deep Dives ## Introduction Hey everyone, it's Phoebe here! I have some great updates to share with you when it comes to animation. So, let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Accessing the Animation Editor I have my window open here, and I'm going to get into my animation. First, I'll go to the very top part of my toolbar and select **Animation** > **Animation Editor**. If you're wondering how to add animation or anything like that, I've covered that in another deep dive. We’ll do a really quick overview here, but if you're more interested in learning more, check out the other animation deep dives because there's a lot of information that I've shared with you all on how these great updates work. ## Working with the Animation Library Now, I'm going to jump into my library over here and select my avatar, then navigate to **Female Motion**. Let’s just do idle. I mean, we can start with idle; it's fine. Now, I'll just hit **Record**. ## Adjusting the Play Region Okay, so something happened where I recorded up to here because this was my play region, but I've got way more over here. We’ve made a few updates, which is really nice. First, I can extend here and say like **500** and hit **Enter**. What I can do is select my full play region here, right-click on top of it, and select **Clamp Region to Selected Layers**. Now it’s clamped to end here. I can also hold down **Shift**, select both of these, right-click on the play region, and say **Clamp Region to Range to Selected Layers**. I’ll want both the transition and all of this to have work. ## Recording the Animation Now that I've done that, I can hit **Record** again, and it will start recording from here and go all the way over there. Now, I can hit **OK**, and now this is all recorded. What’s nice is that I have two recordings, but don't worry! I can select these two, right-click on both of these garments, and say **Merge Layer**. Then it will merge, and isn’t that great? I can hit **Play** and see all of this. If I want, because I do not have this time, I can simply say **Real Time** over here off to the side with configurations, and then hit **Play** to see all of that. ## Customizing the Interface Great! I also have the option of having more or less; I can increase this so that I can see more here, which I kind of have always liked doing. This is not new; it has been there for a while. What is new is that I can also hide my configurations over here. I can hover over the black line, click, and move this in to make it much smaller. I can also adjust other sections to increase their size as well. This is really helpful because now I don’t have to have my configurations take up the entire side, but I can still see it, which is nice. ## New Light Render Animation Feature Now, onto the next update. In our last improvement, you could add animation with these great options. Now, we have the ability to add **Light Render Animation**. I can turn on my dome light and play around with all of this kind of light animation. For instance, I could say, "Right here, I'm going to add this active keyframe, this intensity, and this angle." I’ll move over here and turn on auto keyframes because this is just easier. I’ll uncheck this, move over, and then check this back on, changing the intensity to **3** and the angle to **25**. Now, I can check this back to **1** and **0**. Great! This will be all set. Note that you do have to be in render mode to see all of this happen and to view it. We’ll just render this out and see that. ## Conclusion It is really nice because now you have all of this control over your lights and how it will look, which is really, really fun. Also, if you want to, you can now go to **File** > **Export** > **GLTF**. You can save your avatar animation, both joint and all of that, which is really nice. You can do light render animations, which has always been there, but now you can have your avatar animations as well, which is really, really cool. Thank you all so much for watching! If you have any questions, use that comment section down below. Don’t forget to like and subscribe, and keep having fun in Clo! ```
